nahw.summary: A word that names a person, place, thing, quality or idea.
A word that expresses an action or occurrence and is connected to time.
A particle whose full grammatical meaning appears through its relationship with other words.
nahw.example_en: There is a book in the house.

nahw.summary: A word whose ending can change because of its grammatical position.
A word whose ending normally remains fixed despite changes in grammatical position.
The nominative grammatical state, commonly marked by ḍammah.
The accusative grammatical state, commonly marked by fatḥah.
The genitive state for nouns, commonly marked by kasrah.
The jussive state of the present verb after certain particles.
The opening noun or topic of a nominal sentence and is normally marfūʿ.
The information given about the mubtadaʾ and is normally marfūʿ.
The doer of the action in a verbal sentence and is normally marfūʿ.
The noun affected by the action; the direct object is normally manṣūb.
In a passive sentence, the deputy subject takes the place of the omitted doer and is marfūʿ.
The first noun in an iḍāfah construction; it is linked to the noun after it.
The second noun in an iḍāfah construction and is always majrūr.
An adjective describing a noun. نَعْتٌ and صِفَةٌ are commonly used for the adjective; it follows the noun it describes in key grammatical features such as iʿrāb, definiteness, gender and number.
The noun being described by a naʿt/ṣifah. مَنْعُوتٌ and مَوْصُوفٌ are common terms for the described noun.
A normally manṣūb word describing the state of someone or something during an action.
A normally manṣūb noun that clarifies an otherwise vague quantity or relationship.
nahw.example_en: I bought a litre of water.

nahw.summary: A definite noun referring to something specific or identified.
An indefinite noun referring to a non-specific person or thing.
A word referring to one person or thing.
A form referring to two people or things.
A form referring to three or more.
The masculine grammatical gender.
The feminine grammatical gender.
A pronoun that stands in place of a noun.
A demonstrative expression used to point to something near or far.
A relative expression that links a noun to a following clause.
A noun expressing time or place in relation to an action.
nahw.example_en: I sat in front of the house.

nahw.summary: A preposition that causes the following noun to become majrūr.
Coordination linking one word or phrase to another.
A follower that replaces, restates or clarifies the noun before it. The badal follows the mubdal minhu in iʿrāb.
nahw.example_en: Your brother Zayd came — زَيْدٌ is the badal and أَخُوكَ is the mubdal minhu.

nahw.summary: A follower used to strengthen or emphasise the meaning of the word before it.
A construction excluding something from a preceding general statement.
A conditional construction linking a condition to its result.
nahw.example_en: If you study, you will succeed.

nahw.summary: A construction used to negate a statement or action.
A construction used to ask a question.

nahw.english: Mubdal minhu — the word replaced by the badal
nahw.summary: The noun that comes before the badal and is then restated, clarified or replaced by it. The badal follows the mubdal minhu in grammatical case.
nahw.example_en: Your brother Zayd came — أَخُوكَ is the mubdal minhu and زَيْدٌ is the badal.

nahw.summary: A mubtadaʾ that appears after its khabar instead of at the beginning of the nominal sentence. It remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — رَجُلٌ is the delayed mubtadaʾ.

nahw.summary: A khabar that is placed before the mubtadaʾ. It is often a prepositional phrase or adverbial expression.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is the fronted khabar.

nahw.summary: A particle of negation. In its basic use it negates a statement but does not make the present verb manṣūb or majzūm.
A particle of negation, jussive governance and past meaning. It makes the following present-tense verb majzūm while giving the sentence a past negative meaning.
nahw.example_en: Zayd did not go — يَذْهَبْ is majzūm after لَمْ.

nahw.summary: A particle used to negate. In the basic present-tense use, it does not make the verb manṣūb or majzūm, so the verb normally remains marfūʿ.
nahw.example_en: Zayd does not go — يَذْهَبُ remains marfūʿ.

nahw.summary: A particle of future negation and naṣb. It makes the following present-tense verb manṣūb.
nahw.example_en: Zayd will not go — يَذْهَبَ is manṣūb after لَنْ.

nahw.english: Effect of negation particles on iʿrāb
nahw.summary: Different particles affect the following verb differently: مَا and لَا النَّافِيَةُ normally do not change the iʿrāb of the present verb; لَمْ makes it majzūm; and لَنْ makes it manṣūb.
nahw.example: لَا يَذْهَبُ، لَمْ يَذْهَبْ، لَنْ يَذْهَبَ.
nahw.example_en: He does not go; he did not go; he will not go — showing marfūʿ, majzūm and manṣūb forms.

nahw.summary: A phrase that functions like part of a sentence without being a complete sentence by itself. In Nahw, the most common types are a prepositional phrase (جارّ ومجرور) and an adverbial phrase (ظرف). It often functions as a khabar or relates to a verb.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is shibh al-jumlah and functions as a fronted khabar.

nahw.english: Mutaʿalliq — the word a phrase is connected to
nahw.summary: The word or meaning that a shibh al-jumlah is grammatically connected to. A جارّ ومجرور or ظرف usually depends on a verb, an adjective, a verbal noun, or an understood word such as a hidden khabar.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — فِي الْبَيْتِ is shibh al-jumlah and its mutaʿalliq is an understood khabar such as كَائِنٌ or مُسْتَقِرٌّ.

nahw.summary: The part of the sentence that is attributed to or stated about the musnad ilayh. In a simple nominal sentence, the khabar is the musnad; in a verbal sentence, the verb is commonly treated as the musnad.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student — طَالِبٌ is the musnad.

nahw.english: Musnad ilayh — subject / what the statement is about
nahw.summary: The word or element to which the musnad is attributed. In a nominal sentence, the mubtadaʾ is the musnad ilayh; in a verbal sentence, the fāʿil or its equivalent fills this role.
nahw.example_en: Zayd is a student — زَيْدٌ is the musnad ilayh.

nahw.summary: A word or element that is omitted from the spoken or written sentence but is understood from the grammar or context. In analysis, it is often supplied mentally to explain the structure.
nahw.example_en: There is a man in the house — the khabar can be understood as a maḥdhūf word such as كَائِنٌ or مُسْتَقِرٌّ.
